findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed changing tasks during food preparation without washing hands. The employee was observed preparing coffee, wiping the coffee nozzle with sanitizer, and repeatedly scooping ice from the ice bin to prepare beverages without washing hands between tasks. The person-in-charged (PIC) was informed that this practice may result in contamination, including potential chemical contamination if sanitizer residue remains on hands when handling ice and preparing beverages. CORRECTED: The PIC was instructed by the inspector to review proper handwashing procedures with employees and the employee washed hands before continuing task. Ensure employees wash their hands when changing tasks during food preparation, especially after using sanitizer to wipe the coffee nozzle to prevent food contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: The three ice bins at the server station were observed uncovered during the inspection and not all three bins were being used at the same time. Food residue was observed along the top corner edges of each ice bin. CORRECTED: The inspector instructed the PIC to keep the ice bins covered when not actively in use. Ensure ice bins are kept covered when not actively in use to prevent contamination of ice.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the three compartment sink without caulking. PIC was made aware and PIC ensured inspector that the three compartment sink will have the necessary caulking done.  Ensure that the three compartment sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector observe that there was only one employee with proof of food handler certification at the facility during the inspection. PIC said that everyone else does have valid food handler certifications however, was unable to provide proof as they may have been locked in a cabinet that is not accessible to them. PIC does not have access to the digital copies either. PIC ensured inspector that they will have the certifications printed out  making them available when needed. Ensure that all employees with the exception of those of the certified food protection manager certification acquired their food handler certification within 30 days of employment.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: Facility is out of temperature dots to verify dish machine temperature. Provide maximum registering thermometer or paper thermometer for the verification of dish machine sanitizing temperature. A follow up will be conducted. Ensure that the facility has a way to verify the dish machine temperature.

(A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Facility does not have a written procedure for the employees to follow when responding to vomit or diarrheal incidents. Provide a written procedure that is readily accessible for the person in charge (pic). The PIC figured out how to put in the ticket or make the call in order to alert the company of their need for service. The PIC is currently doing a written procedure to add to the public health binder when created so that the facility remains in compliance. The violation was corrected on site.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Sanitizer bucket at the front drive thru area tested at 100 ppm. Employee changed out sani buckets upon request. 400 ppm from the quat at the 3 compartment sink. Discussed frequent changes of sanitizer with employee and the use of warm/hot water for sanitation. COS.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

Inspector observed a personal bottled drink stored in the refrigeration unit with food for sale to the public. The bottled drink was discarded in the garbage. Do not store personal food items in product coolers. The violation was corrected on site.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no certified food protection manager on site during the inspection. Ensure facility is staffed with enough CFPM’s to have one during all hours of operation. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed employee to improperly wash hands - no barrier was used to turn off the faucet. Ensure employees are aware of proper handwashing techniques. Ensure a barrier such as a paper towel is used to turn off the faucets. Discussed with employee and PIC. COS.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. 

Observed no heat test strips or a maximum registering thermometer for the facility. Ensure facility has a manner to test the surface temperature of utensils within the heated dish machine. Machine was registering at 169 degrees F. Inspector will follow-up on 3/14/22.
